faults.title: Remove default gateway
observableSymptoms: Traffic that depends on the default route may lose external reachability while local state remains otherwise unchanged.
faults.hiddenTruth: The target resource's modeled default gateway has been removed.
learningObjectives: Verify default-route configuration before changing unrelated services.

faults.title: Set wrong default gateway
observableSymptoms: Local-subnet communication may still work while off-subnet traffic follows a non-existent or incorrect next hop.
faults.hiddenTruth: The modeled default gateway was replaced with a deterministic incorrect documentation-prefix address.
learningObjectives: Separate local-link reachability from default-route reachability and verify the configured gateway.

faults.title: Blackhole primary route
observableSymptoms: A destination covered by the first modeled route becomes deterministically unreachable even though the interface and neighboring devices may remain healthy.
faults.hiddenTruth: The first modeled route action was changed to blackhole.
learningObjectives: Identify an explicit blackhole route instead of troubleshooting unrelated DNS or application services.

faults.title: Set wrong route next hop
observableSymptoms: The route still exists, but traffic may be forwarded toward a next hop that is not the declared neighbor.
faults.hiddenTruth: The first modeled route was retained but its next-hop value was replaced with an incorrect address.
learningObjectives: Check route destination, next hop and neighboring topology together rather than treating route presence as sufficient.

faults.title: Disable primary route
observableSymptoms: The first route remains visible in configuration data but is no longer eligible for forwarding.
faults.hiddenTruth: The first modeled route was administratively disabled.
learningObjectives: Verify route administrative state as well as destination and next hop.

faults.title: Replace VLAN membership
observableSymptoms: The endpoint can remain link-up yet lose Layer-2 compatibility with links that require its original VLAN.
faults.hiddenTruth: The target VLAN membership list was replaced with a deterministic wrong VLAN.
learningObjectives: Distinguish physical/link-up state from VLAN membership and broadcast-domain reachability.

faults.title: Set wrong access VLAN
observableSymptoms: A port or endpoint can appear operational while frames are placed in the wrong broadcast domain.
faults.hiddenTruth: The modeled access/native VLAN value was changed to an incorrect VLAN ID.
learningObjectives: Verify the VLAN assigned to an access endpoint when link state alone looks healthy.

faults.title: Disable switch port
observableSymptoms: The modeled switch port is administratively down; higher-layer configuration may still look correct.
faults.hiddenTruth: The switch port administrative state was set down.
learningObjectives: Check administrative port state before investigating higher network layers.

faults.title: Force STP blocking state
observableSymptoms: The link can remain physically up while the modeled spanning-tree state prevents ordinary forwarding.
faults.hiddenTruth: The modeled switch port spanning-tree state was forced to blocking.
learningObjectives: Recognize that an up link can intentionally stop forwarding because of spanning-tree state.

faults.title: Restrict trunk allowed VLANs
observableSymptoms: Only a subset of expected VLANs remains allowed across the modeled trunk, producing selective reachability failures.
faults.hiddenTruth: The trunk allowed-VLAN list was deterministically reduced to one VLAN.
learningObjectives: Use selective cross-VLAN symptoms to inspect trunk allowed-VLAN configuration.

faults.title: Replace DNS resolvers
observableSymptoms: IP connectivity may remain intact while hostname lookups time out or query an unintended resolver.
faults.hiddenTruth: The target resolver list was replaced with a deterministic unreachable/wrong documentation-prefix resolver.
learningObjectives: Test name resolution separately from raw IP reachability and inspect resolver configuration.

faults.title: Remove all DNS resolvers
observableSymptoms: Direct IP connections may work while normal hostname-based access fails immediately because no resolver is configured.
faults.hiddenTruth: The target resolver list was emptied.
learningObjectives: Confirm that at least one resolver is configured before investigating authoritative DNS.

faults.title: Set wrong DNS search domain
observableSymptoms: Fully-qualified names may resolve while short hostnames fail or resolve in an unintended suffix.
faults.hiddenTruth: The client DNS search-domain list was replaced with an incorrect suffix.
learningObjectives: Compare short-name and FQDN behavior and inspect the DNS suffix/search list.

faults.title: Disable DNS server
observableSymptoms: Clients configured to use this resolver may lose all answers even though network reachability to the server remains.
faults.hiddenTruth: The modeled DNS service was disabled.
learningObjectives: Separate server reachability from DNS service availability.

faults.title: Corrupt primary DNS record
observableSymptoms: DNS queries can succeed syntactically but direct clients to the wrong address, creating an application-looking failure.
faults.hiddenTruth: The address in the first modeled DNS record was replaced with an incorrect documentation-prefix address.
learningObjectives: Verify returned DNS data, not only whether the DNS query itself succeeds.

faults.title: Disable DHCP client
observableSymptoms: The endpoint stops accepting modeled DHCP configuration; stale or missing addressing can then dominate symptoms.
faults.hiddenTruth: The modeled DHCP client was disabled.
learningObjectives: Check whether the client is actually configured to obtain settings from DHCP.

faults.title: Set wrong DHCP gateway option
observableSymptoms: A client can receive a lease and local connectivity yet fail off-subnet because the leased gateway is wrong.
faults.hiddenTruth: The modeled DHCP gateway option was replaced with an incorrect address.
learningObjectives: Inspect individual DHCP lease options rather than treating any successful lease as valid configuration.

faults.title: Set wrong DHCP DNS option
observableSymptoms: The lease succeeds and IP routing can work while hostname resolution fails because DHCP supplied the wrong resolver.
faults.hiddenTruth: The modeled DHCP DNS option was replaced with an incorrect resolver list.
learningObjectives: Trace a DNS symptom back to the DHCP option that supplied the resolver configuration.

faults.title: Set wrong DHCP prefix length
observableSymptoms: The client may misclassify remote hosts as local or local hosts as remote, producing confusing ARP/routing behavior.
faults.hiddenTruth: The modeled DHCP subnet-prefix option was replaced with an incorrect prefix length.
learningObjectives: Verify subnet mask/prefix semantics when same-subnet and routed reachability disagree.

faults.title: Exhaust DHCP server pool
observableSymptoms: New clients cannot obtain a lease while existing clients with valid leases may continue working.
faults.hiddenTruth: The modeled DHCP server available-lease count was reduced to zero.
learningObjectives: Use the difference between existing and new clients to identify DHCP pool exhaustion.

faults.title: Force default deny policy
observableSymptoms: Flows not explicitly permitted by modeled ACL rules may be blocked.
faults.hiddenTruth: The target resource's default ACL action has been changed to deny.
learningObjectives: Distinguish policy-default behavior from explicit rule behavior.

faults.title: Set firewall default action to deny
observableSymptoms: Flows without a matching allow rule are denied while explicitly allowed traffic can remain unaffected.
faults.hiddenTruth: The Engine-visible firewall defaultAction was changed to deny.
learningObjectives: Distinguish explicit rules from the policy applied to unmatched traffic.

faults.title: Disable primary firewall rule
observableSymptoms: Traffic that depended on the first allow rule may now fall through to later rules or the default policy.
faults.hiddenTruth: The first modeled firewall rule was administratively disabled.
learningObjectives: Verify rule enablement and ordered fall-through, not only that a rule object exists.

faults.title: Disable primary DNAT rule
observableSymptoms: Inbound traffic reaches the firewall but no longer receives the expected destination/port translation.
faults.hiddenTruth: The first modeled DNAT rule was disabled.
learningObjectives: Differentiate firewall allow policy from DNAT translation availability.

faults.title: Set wrong DNAT translated port
observableSymptoms: The external port-forward still matches, but traffic is translated to a backend port where the expected service may not listen.
faults.hiddenTruth: The first DNAT rule translatedPort was changed to an incorrect deterministic port.
learningObjectives: Compare external and translated service ports when a port-forward appears present but the service remains unreachable.
